advice: Abstain. The supplied `gemm` fast path calls the whole generated LIBXSMM kernel; its internal K loops in `Llibxsmm_478` and `Llibxsmm_70c` are not safely editable in this experiment without changing generated code. The obvious reuse schedule—load `z0/z1` and `z2/z3`, issue all four current FMOPA operations, then advance `x0` and `x3`—was already measured as `libxsmm-k-loop-consume-before-pointer-updates`. No distinct, legal input-vector reuse change is supported by the supplied evidence without changing the ZA tile or generated loop structure. Keep the current source unchanged; do not repeat the measured schedule.
risks: The measured schedule was not promoted, and its paired scores were mixed. They do not establish that pointer-update placement caused the outcome. Proposing another reuse scheme without a concrete source mapping risks register pressure or relying on extra FP32 ZA tiles, which are not established here. If a distinct implementation is proposed later, check full GEMM correctness, general sizes, tails and n<=0 under the fixed ABI and tolerance, then use fresh paired controls with the power mode unchanged. No performance gain is established.
